subsystems.name: Electrode array
subsystems.role: picks up the tiny voltages that motor neurons generate in the forearm muscles.

subsystems.name: Analogue front end
subsystems.role: amplifies and cleans signals of a few microvolts while rejecting mains hum and movement noise.

subsystems.name: Motion and context sensing
subsystems.role: lets the decoder separate intended gestures from arm movement and changing posture.

subsystems.name: Decoder
subsystems.role: turns the multi-channel signal into an intended hand gesture or continuous control.

subsystems.name: Compute, power and radio
subsystems.role: runs the model on the wrist and sends the result to a headset, phone or computer.

buildSteps.title: Design the electrode band
buildSteps.detail: Electrodes are arranged around the forearm to sit over the muscles that move the fingers and wrist, on a comfortable, repeatable fit.

buildSteps.title: Build the analogue front end
buildSteps.detail: Each channel amplifies microvolt-level signals, filters out low-frequency motion artefacts and high-frequency noise, and digitises the result.

buildSteps.title: Collect training data
buildSteps.detail: Volunteers perform many gestures and finer movements while their signals are recorded, synchronised with what they were asked to do.

buildSteps.title: Train the decoder
buildSteps.detail: A model learns the mapping from electrode patterns to intended movement, using data from many people so it can generalise.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the individual
buildSteps.detail: A short personalised session adapts the model to the user's anatomy, electrode contact and resting state.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the wearable
buildSteps.detail: Processor, battery and radio are packaged into a wristband that stays comfortable and keeps good skin contact.

buildSteps.title: Validate in realistic use
buildSteps.detail: The band is tested for latency, accuracy and fatigue in tasks such as menu selection, typing or controlling a cursor.

prerequisites.why: without stable skin contact the signal drifts and the decoder degrades.
the model must run for a day on a small battery.
generalisation across people and sessions is the main unsolved problem.
reading intent before visible movement requires better signal models and more data.
input feels wrong if the gesture is decoded instantly but arrives late.

pathway.milestone: research prototypes from Meta's Reality Labs and others read several distinct gestures and simple continuous control from a wristband
pathway.unlocks: hands-free input for AR/VR and accessibility use cases.

pathway.milestone: consumer devices ship with a wristband as a companion input to glasses or phones
pathway.unlocks: everyday gesture control without cameras watching the hands.

pathway.milestone: decoders that need little or no per-session calibration
pathway.unlocks: reliable use across users, sweat, fatigue and changing electrode positions.

pathway.milestone: higher-bandwidth signals decoded from individual motor units
pathway.unlocks: fine control such as typing or manipulating virtual objects with intent alone.
